Synopsis:
A nature diary piece describing the discovery of a stranded Velella velella (by-the-wind sailor), a pelagic hydrozoan, on a UK estuarine beach. The article notes unusual summer strandings along the Welsh coast and Cumbria, typically a winter phenomenon, attributed to calmer waters and favourable winds. A passing reference is made to record-high sea surface temperatures as context for the species' UV-protective pigmentation.
